blocks.text: Zero trust microsegmentation offers flexibility for per-device segmentation while continuing to reduce attack surfaces.

Zero Trust Branch appliances are used to create highly granular subnetworks called micro-subnets with small IP address ranges (e.g., /27 to /30) within existing virtual local area networks (VLANs) and add endpoints that require direct L2 connectivity to these micro-subnets. Devices within a micro-subnet communicate directly, while traffic between different micro-subnets or external destinations is routed through the Zero Trust Branch gateway for inspection and controlled by enforcing policies.
To configure micro-subnets, complete the following steps in the Zscaler Admin Console:

blocks.item: 1. Configure Zero Trust Branch as a DHCP server.
From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites.
On the Sites page, click the required site in the Site Name column.
See image.
Click the Settings tab and in the left-side panel, select DHCP Service.
See image.
For DHCP Service, select DHCP Server from the drop-down menu.
Click Save.
2. Add VLAN and enable Airgap+.
Go to Zero Trust Branch > Deployments > Sites
On the Sites page, click the required site in the Site Name column.
Click the VLANs tab.
For the required Airgap VLAN, click the Gear icon and select Edit.
See image.
In the Edit Airgap VLAN window:
Enable Airgap+: Enable and enter the following details in the fields that appear:
Netmask: Select the subnet mask that must be used to determine the network scope for the asset in Airgap+ mode.
Airgap+ Range Start: Enter the network address of the first micro-subnet.
Airgap+ Range End: Enter the broadcast address of the last micro-subnet.

While adding the VLAN to create a micro-subnet, the Airgap range cannot overlap with Airgap+. For example, 10.90.10.8 to 10.90.10.23 defines the range for /29 micro-subnets. 10.90.10.x/24 endpoints outside Airgap+ range are assigned with /32 IP addresses.
See image.
Click Save.
This configuration creates the following two micro-subnets:
Airgap+ is suited for deployments where:
Some endpoints cannot get a /32 mask.
The device IP address is flexible, because it must fit into the microsegments available for endpoints defined by the Airgap+ configuration.
If the device IP address is not flexible, use Airgap-Lite by changing the security protection at the asset level.
To change the security protection:
From the navigation menu, go to Zero Trust Branch > Dashboard > Asset Intelligence.
On the Assets page, select the checkbox for the required Device, then click Edit.
Select Network from the Segmentation Granularity drop-down menu.
Click Save.
3. Update assets using a CSV file.
Go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Edge > Sites.
On the Sites page, click the required site in the Site Name column.
Click the VLANs tab.
For the required Airgap VLAN, click the Gear icon and select Import Endpoints CSV.
See image.
In the Import Endpoints CSV window, upload a CSV file. You can also download the template and use it to add the endpoints and then upload the CSV file.
See image.

Click Validate to verify the imported data and view the details. Note that the IP addresses for the Airgap+ endpoints (vlan10-dev3 and vlan10-dev4) are used from the CSV file. For the endpoints that are not part of the micro-subnet (vlan10-dev1 and vlan10-dev2), the IP address field is empty and the /32 IP address is assigned by the DHCP server.
Click Submit.
In the confirmation window that appears, read the message and click Confirm.
See image.
4. Verify assets.
Go to Infrastructure > Connectors > Edge > Assets.
On the Assets page, you can see that the assets in the micro-subnet (as per the imported CSV) are assigned with /29 IP addresses.
5. Create a network object group.
To create a network type object group for devices in the micro-subnet:
Go to Zero Trust Branch > Resources > Objects.
On the Objects page, click Add, then select Network from the list.
See image.
In the Add Network window:
Name: Enter a name for the network.
Add a CIDR block or FQDN and click +Add.
Member Groups: Select the groups from the drop-down menu.
See image.
Click Add.
6. Create a firewall policy.
Create a firewall policy to restrict the Airgap+ endpoints' communication within the micro-subnets. To learn more, see Understanding Firewall Policies.
